actionable.title: Reject an explicitly empty receipt path before preflight or tool probes
actionable.problem: Both wrapper allowlists accept --write=. Argparse records its value as an empty string, but main checks if args.write rather than whether the option was supplied. The empty target therefore bypasses receipt_target and is silently treated as no write request. With an otherwise valid synthetic baseline, preflight returns 0 and final verification runs Node/Pi/uv probes and returns 0 without creating the requested receipt. This violates the documented invalid-write-path exit-2 contract and the promise that preflight checks a supplied --write path. The same truthiness pattern also controls candidate mode and its incompatible-option checks.
actionable.fix: Treat supplied path options as present when they are not None and reject empty values before mode selection or any tool probes. Route every supplied --write through receipt_target, apply the same explicit-presence validation to --write-policy-candidate and its exclusivity checks, and add focused regressions for --write= and empty separate values through the verifier and both wrappers. An invalid target should exit 2 and prevent subsequent probes and installation.
reproduction: Use the existing scripts/bootstrap/test_policy_baseline.py PolicyBaselineTests fixture; setUp(), then digest = write_manifest() to obtain its explicitly synthetic approval and pin.
Call invoke_preflight("--policy-manifest", str(case.manifest), "--policy-manifest-sha256", digest, "--write="). Observed exit 0, policy_preflight_ok true, and no docs/evidence output directory.

Wrap case.case.fake_run to record calls, then call case.case.invoke with the same arguments. Observed exit 0, mocked node --version / pi --version / uv --version calls, and no receipt. The reproduction used the existing synthetic harness and no real package or agent commands.
